title: Anchored publish cadence and automated re-verification playbook for performance profiles
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Background: As the model catalog grows, teams need a deterministic, auditable schedule for publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) and an automated re-verification workflow that minimizes stale pins and surprise regressions. This ticket defines an anchored cadence (weekly / monthly tiers), an automated refresh trigger playbook based on telemetry and sampling, and an artifact signing/ledger so consumers can trust profile provenance.

Goals:
- Define publish cadence tiers (rapid / standard / archival) with clear acceptance gates per tier.
- Implement an automated re-verification pipeline that runs lightweight sample-driven checks daily and full verification on thresholded drift or scheduled windows.
- Produce signed profile artifacts (fingerprint + attestation) stored in the canonical registry with rollback metadata.
- Establish SLOs and KPIs for profile freshness, false-negative drift detection, and time-to-rollforward when a profile is invalidated.

Scope: covers the publish orchestration, re-verification triggers, signature artifacts, and runbook for automated rollbacks/rollforwards. Integration work with runtime (telemetry contracts), CI/dataset harness, and console UI for profile state are in scope. Out of scope: model training/selection and on-device/hardware-specific kernel changes.

Non-goals: building full model benchmarking from scratch; this relies on the existing verification harness but augments scheduling, sampling, and artifact signing.

Success metrics:
- 95% of production-facing profiles have an up-to-date verification within their tier window.
- Drift-trigger false-positive rate <5% measured over 90 days.
- Mean time from drift detection to published rollback or refreshed profile < 6 hours for P0 customer-impacting regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Publish cadence matrix (rapid/standard/archival) documented and agreed by stakeholders
Automated daily lightweight verification job implemented and running against a rolling sample of logged inference requests
Full verification pipeline runnable on-demand with artifact signing and an immutable fingerprint stored in the canonical registry
Console shows profile state (verified, stale, drifted) and links to the signed artifact and verification run details
Rollback and rollforward runbook codified and validated with a tabletop exercise and follow-up action items
implementation_notes: Telemetry contract: runtime must emit sample hashes and aggregated latency histograms to the verification queue; work tracked in ENG-70512
Sampling: use stratified sampling by model variant, region, and route to avoid operational bias on cost-sensitive endpoints
Verification levels: lightweight (prefix microbench + production sample checks) and full (end-to-end benchmark with canonical prompts and throughput runs)
Artifact: JSON profile + canonical benchmark bundle + signature (ed25519) and provenance metadata (runtime version, kernel selection, quantization flags)
Storage: registry entries are content-addressed; earlier version must remain retrievable for at least 180 days
Rollback: automated flagging of dependent pins and optional canary rollback to next-compatible pinned profile
open_questions: What thresholds should trigger full verification vs. scheduled refresh? (latency p95 change percentage, error-rate delta, cost-per-token deviation)
Who signs artifacts for enterprise private deployments (Redwood CA vs. customer KMS integration)?
How to surface transient infra-induced latency spikes vs. true model performance regressions?
Should archival-tier profiles be prunable automatically after 365 days with notification to owners?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy telemetry leads to frequent false positives. Mitigation: require multi-metric consensus (latency + error-rate + cost) before firing a full verification job.
Risk: automated rollbacks could produce user-facing regressions. Mitigation: require canary confirmation window and human review for profiles with customer_impact==high.
Risk: signature provenance complexity across Private deployments. Mitigation: implement pluggable signer interface and document customer KMS onboarding flow.
